architecture_decisions: Build two independent firmware ELFs with separate CMake configurations, startup/vector/MSP/data/bss/heap/timebase/OS/HAL tick and ABI; orchestrate them with one checked pair manifest. Do not combine CM4 and CM7 objects or OS kernels into one runtime.

M7 reference boot owner coordinates global supply/RCC/clock/Flash/common resets and peer launch; M4 per-core SystemInit must not reset global clocks. A core-local platform stop cannot disable a peer-owned timer, DMA, HSEM, SRAM or system source.

Select one reviewed physical shared SRAM window only after reference-manual reachability and alias checks. Header D2_AHBSRAM0x30000000 and D3_SRAM0x38000000 are candidates, not admitted sizes/addresses. Exclude private TCM and stacks by default; each image linker reserves shared bytes once outside bss clearing and ordinary allocator placement.

First reference transport uses explicitly verified noncacheable shared control and payload attributes on M7 and compatible M4 access; keep release/acquire barriers. Later cached payload is a separate mode with complete-line clean/invalidate plus its own evidence. HSEM locks/doorbells are not cache coherency mechanisms.

A lane remains unidirectional; bidirectional traffic uses two statically distinct lanes. HSEM channel ownership and notification IRQ routing are explicit. Doorbell coalescing/loss only affects wake hints; publication/ACK predicates remain authoritative and service can make bounded progress.

Keep one physical peripheral owner, including its DMA and IRQ. Avoid fine-grained cross-core locks in normal peripheral hot paths; cross-core services exchange offsets/lengths in shared windows, never local pointers or executable function pointers.

Do not implement stopped as peer-epoch change, heartbeat timeout, HSEM release or a core reset request alone. Reset join stays unsupported until the exact old CPU, DMA, IRQ and all payload observers are proved unable to resume accessing the lane.

An authoritative boot owner must persistently reject reused/decreasing epochs across warm and whole-chip resets as the existing contract requires. A freshly zeroed shared RAM counter or volatile static does not satisfy this. First hardware acceptance requires a reviewed retained/provisioned identity design or power-fail-safe persistent counter with wear/Flash safety evidence; do not weaken the common API.
